item.title: US soldier Jian Zhao admits selling military information to Chinese buyers
item.description: An American soldier who sold what he claimed was top secret know-how to Chinese-linked buyers faces up to a decade in prison after admitting passing on sensitive military information. Army sergeant Jian Zhao, 37, took advantage of his security clearance to get his hands on restricted documents. He snapped pictures of military information on his mobile phone and offered to sell military computers and government hard drives, as well as details about communications networks, rocket and missile...

item.title: Home advantage: can Hong Kong turn sports bodies’ arrival into global influence?

item.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says he is in therapy, as comeback rally fades
item.description: Jensen Huang apologised to Nvidia staff and said he was in therapy on Tuesday, as a stock rally triggered by his shock return as CEO faltered amid persistent doubts over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom. “I made some terrible mistakes,” Huang told an hour-long all-hands meeting at the company’s Santa Clara, California, headquarters, The New York Times reported after reviewing a live stream of the event. item.title: Why Asia’s AI rally faces a tougher road even after Jensen Huang’s comeback
item.description: While Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia has soothed market sentiment, analysts have warned that the artificial intelligence boom that propelled Asian chip stocks this year is unlikely to regain its first-half momentum – and that US regulatory scrutiny of the sector remains far from over. “The market is certainly, at least for a day, soothed by the fact that Jensen is back,” said Brian Levitt, chief global market strategist at investment management firm Invesco, at a media briefing on...

item.title: Brazil’s ‘Lithium Valley’ makes its play for BYD as three states fight over new EV plant
item.description: Chinese carmaker BYD said on Tuesday it will sign a memorandum of understanding with Brazil’s Minas Gerais state in January as it weighs where to build a factory for electric buses, trucks and vans that Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro are also trying to attract.
